story.iWant: to record my screen with a single click
story.soThat: I can capture tutorials and demonstrations quickly
story.tasks: - Implement screen source acquisition (AC: 1, 2) - Implement microphone audio capture (AC: 3) - Create MediaRecorder for screen (AC: 4) - Implement recording start flow (AC: 5, 6) - Implement recording stop flow (AC: 7, 8, 9) - Implement file writing logic (AC: 8) - Implement error handling (AC: 10) - Implement comprehensive logging (AC: 11) - Manage recording state (AC: 12) - Write integration tests - Test with real recording

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: RecordingService.startRecording() handles 'screen' mode with auto-selected primary screen
Screen capture stream obtained using Electron's desktopCapturer API with auto-selected source
Microphone audio automatically captured and mixed with screen recording
MediaRecorder instance created with WebM/VP9 codec at 1920x1080, 30fps, 8Mbps
Recording starts immediately after mode selection (within 2 seconds per NFR)
Recorded chunks buffered in memory during capture
All MediaStream tracks properly stopped and cleaned up on recording end
Recording saved to temp directory as `screen-recording-[timestamp].webm`
RecordingService.stopRecording() returns file path and metadata (duration, resolution)
Error handling for screen permission denial with actionable user message
Logging with [Recording] prefix for all screen recording operations
Recording state properly managed (isRecording flag, currentMode='screen')

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Complete flow from user clicks to auto-import. Auto-selects primary screen via desktopCapturer, records with MediaRecorder, saves WebM, auto-imports to media library, auto-places on Track 1.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Screen defaults: 1920x1080 resolution, 30fps frameRate, 8Mbps videoBitsPerSecond. Microphone audio with echoCancellation and noiseSuppression enabled.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Recording start latency must be within 2 seconds. No frame drops maintaining 30fps. UI remains responsive during recording.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: App must request macOS screen recording permissions with clear user guidance. MediaStream tracks must be explicitly stopped on completion.

doc.title: Decision Architecture
doc.snippet: desktopCapturer for screen recording, MediaRecorder API for capturing to WebM.

artifact.reason: Foundation from Story 5.1 - extends with screen recording implementation including getPrimaryScreen, startRecording(mode='screen'), MediaRecorder management, and file saving

node.package: Provides desktopCapturer API for screen source enumeration and capture

constraints.constraint: Must use Electron desktopCapturer API for screen source acquisition
Must use native MediaRecorder API for recording (no external libraries)
Auto-select primary screen = first screen from desktopCapturer.getSources()
No user screen selection dialog - fully automatic
Must start recording within 2 seconds of mode selection (NFR)
WebM format with VP9 codec (fallback to VP8 if unavailable)
Microphone audio automatically captured and mixed
Chunks buffered with 5s timeslice for crash recovery
All MediaStream tracks must be stopped to release resources
Must handle macOS screen recording permission gracefully

tests.standards: Unit tests with mocked Electron desktopCapturer and MediaRecorder APIs. Test error paths for permissions, no devices, busy devices. Verify fallback logic without actual hardware. Integration tests for service initialization. Manual testing required for actual screen capture and file playback.

ideas.idea: Mock desktopCapturer.getSources() to return array of screen sources, verify getPrimaryScreen selects first
Test getUserMedia called with correct chromeMediaSource and chromeMediaSourceId constraints
Test microphone audio stream merging into screen MediaStream
Test MediaRecorder instantiation with correct mimeType (webm;codecs=vp9) and videoBitsPerSecond (8000000)
Measure time from startRecording call to mediaRecorder.start() (must be <2s)
Test ondataavailable handler collects chunks into array
Test all video and audio tracks stopped on stopRecording
Test RecordingOutput structure with file path, duration, resolution metadata
Test NotAllowedError handling displays "enable in System Preferences" message
Verify all console.log calls include [Recording] prefix
Test state transitions: isRecording false→true on start, true→false on stop, currentMode updates
